title: Google Search expands agentic capabilities with information agents and Universal Cart
summary: Google‘s information agents and Universal Cart stand to change how users discover and buy products online.
body_markdown:
Google announced new agentic capabilities coming to Search — including[information agents](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-io-2026/#search-agents:~:text=and%20mobile%2C%20worldwide.-,Search%20agents,-We%E2%80%99re%20entering%20the) that monitor the web on a user's behalf and[Universal Cart](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/shopping/google-shopping-cart/) that aggregates products from multiple retailers and services in one place.


Google made these announcements during Google I/O 2026. Information agents has already rolled out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers this summer. And Universal Cart is now live on Google Search and Gemini in the U.S.


Information agents continuously scan the web after a user's initial query and send back what Elizabeth Reid, VP of Search at Google, called "an intelligent, synthesized update, with the ability to take action."


Robby Stein, VP of Product at Google Search,[posted on X](https://x.com/rmstein/status/2056810017265999910) about this specific update:


Universal Cart promises to be a central hub for shopping on Google. Transactions complete on merchants’ sites, but Google handles price comparison and deal-finding. Shoppers can now set price alerts, get promo codes applied automatically, and check out with Google Pay.


Universal Cart will soon be available for merchants like Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair, and Shopify.


A few related updates are also in motion:


- **Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)** allows users to set guardrails related to things like budget and brand preferences for agentic transactions
- [Agentic booking](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-mode-agentic-restaurant-booking/) is expanding to cover local experiences and services
- **Checkout experiences**[powered by Universal Commerce Protocol](https://www.semrush.com/blog/google-ucp-checkout-in-main-serp/) **(UCP)** are expanding to Canada and Australia, with the U.K. to follow


## What the expanded agentic capabilities mean for marketers


Information agents may reduce[website traffic](https://www.semrush.com/website/) given the agents are doing a lot of the work for users, but the traffic that does come through is likely to be higher intent.


Basically, users who arrive at a website after an agent has already filtered and synthesized results are further along in their decision-making process and may be ready to purchase.


That makes conversion readiness as important as visibility. Priority pages need to be optimized to receive high-intent traffic and move it forward in the buyer’s journey.


For ecommerce brands preparing for[agentic commerce](https://www.semrush.com/blog/agentic-commerce-optimization/) , UCP readiness is the immediate priority.


Universal Cart uses UCP to complete transactions. As Universal Cart expands, you need to have a UCP-enabled store to make it into carts among users shopping across Google. Our[UCP guide](https://www.semrush.com/blog/universal-commerce-protocol/) covers details about how to become eligible.


## How to prepare for agentic commerce


First things first, make sure your store is UCP-enabled. Universal Cart is now live, and stores without UCP support can’t appear in shoppers’ carts.


Then get the fundamentals of agentic search right. Start by optimizing for entity clarity, topical authority, and clear structure. And measure your results to see if you’re improving your AI visibility.
